c: Who am I? — A Freiburg dance academy where an American newcomer arrives in a storm, soon learning her teachers are a coven answering to Helena Markos.

An alchemist raised three homes of stone, / For three dark sisters, each a throne;
The Mother of Shadows rules the one / In New York, beneath a cold gray sun.
“The murderer is in the picture, and you saw it!” A jazz pianist witnesses a killing, then keeps haunting a villa of a screaming child, a mechanical doll and black gloves.
Who am I? — A Latin word for darkness; in Rome, a visiting thriller novelist finds a razor-wielding killer is staging murders straight out of his latest book.

A Swiss school on a windswept height, / Where a girl can call the flies by night;
A glowing insect guides her through, / To find what killer stalks the view.
Who am I? — A decaying Louisiana hotel inherited by a young woman, built over one of the seven gateways of Hell and sealed since a painter was crucified in the cellar.
“Dunwich is a gateway.” A priest hangs himself in a New England graveyard, and a medium in New York dies of fright, seeing the door to the underworld open.
Who am I? — A 1960 Mario Bava picture opening with a Moldavian witch-princess branded and fitted with an iron mask studded with spikes on the inside.

A blind musician, singing war, / Is painted over, ear and pore,
With holy scripture, head to heel — / Yet both his ears the spirits peel.
Who am I? — Two women in a field of tall reeds kill stray soldiers for their armor, until one dons a demon mask that will not come off her face.

A bamboo grove, a burnt-down home, / Two women slain, now spirits roam;
With feline grace and thirst for blood, / They tear through samurai like flood.
“I’m not dead — but I’m so lonely.” Sealed rooms with red tape, shadows burned into walls, and ghosts spreading through the early internet in a Kiyoshi Kurosawa elegy.
Who am I? — A widower stages a fake casting call to find a new wife and meets a quiet woman with a burlap sack, piano wire and a chant of “deeper, deeper”.

A ceiling stain that spreads and grows, / A yellow raincoat, red school bag;
A mother in a custody feud / Finds something wet that’s watching, nude.
“Who are you?” A detective keeps asking an amnesiac drifter, who flicks a lighter and leaves victims carved with a bloody X while ordinary people kill on his suggestion.
Who am I? — A 2003 Korean ghost story in which two girls return from hospital to a lakeside house, a bitter stepmother and a wardrobe holding the family’s secret.
“Rowan Morrison is not here.” A devout police sergeant flies his seaplane to Summerisle over a missing child — and a May Day he’ll never forget.
Who am I? — A grieving restoration expert in Venice glimpses a small figure in a red coat and follows it through narrow canals after his daughter’s drowning.

A governess at a country estate / Believes two children haunted late;
A ghostly valet, a drowned young maid, / Possess the pair, she is afraid.
“Journeys end in lovers meeting.” A 1963 black-and-white tale of four guests in a mansion where the door seems to breathe and a lonely woman hears her name called.
Who am I? — A church organist who survives a drowning car crash, then is stalked by a pale, ghostly man and drawn toward a derelict lakeside pavilion in Utah.

A scrap of parchment, runes aglow, / Is slipped to him — and he will know;
Three days remain until the fire-beast comes / To stalk a skeptic through the slums.
“Is it so terrible to be a woman who jumped from a window?” A timid Paris clerk rents the flat of a suicide and begins to turn into her.
Who am I? — Left alone in a London flat, a young manicurist hallucinates arms reaching from the walls and a cracked wall as an uneasy rabbit rots on a plate.
“Can you be my friend? I’m not a girl.” A bullied twelve-year-old in a snowy Swedish suburb befriends an odd new neighbor who must be invited before entering.
Who am I? — A strict vegetarian vet-school freshman, forced into a hazing ritual, who eats a rabbit kidney and awakens a very different appetite.

A plate of steel inside her skull, / A cabaret car’s sensual lull;
A firefighter claims her as his son — / The Palme d’Or went to this one.
Who am I? — A 2008 French film whose long-abused heroine and her best friend face a secretive society seeking glimpses of the afterlife through suffering.
“Open the door.” On Christmas Eve, a widow eight months pregnant is besieged by a woman in black, who has a pair of scissors and an obsession.
Who am I? — Two students retreat to a farmhouse and a rusty truck driver in coveralls shows up, with a tangled twist that rewrites the whole movie.

A sack-faced child at a seaside door, / A lost boy not seen anymore;
A mother seeks him with candle and game, / A treasure hunt that ends in shame.
Who am I? — A woman going blind from a degenerative disease investigates her twin sister’s apparent suicide and is followed by an unseen man.
“Keep filming!” A Barcelona TV reporter and cameraman follow firefighters into an apartment block that’s sealed by the authorities, with something upstairs.

A bomb stands upright in the yard, / A child ghost sighs and whispers hard;
In Spain’s civil war, a school of boys / Learns that the dead keep mournful noise.
Who am I? — A sinking English mansion on a hill of red clay, where an American novelist is courted by a baronet and warned by ghosts to leave.
“Someone’s been looking after you.” Two girls found feral in a cabin after five years are adopted by their uncle, unaware that something has followed them out of the woods.
Who am I? — A 2014 Detroit-set film where a curse passes from person to person and walks toward you slowly, wearing the faces of strangers or loved ones.

A winter cabin, snow piled high, / A cult survivor, two kids nearby;
The power dies, the pills are gone, / And something chilling carries on.
“Don’t play with the board.” In 1991 Madrid, a teenager looking after her siblings tries a Ouija session during a solar eclipse and invites something sinister in.
Who am I? — An unidentified young woman with no outward injuries but a ruined interior is brought to a family morgue; a bell tied to my toe starts ringing.

A schoolgirl trip to a country home, / A grand piano with a tooth-bared dome;
The futon swallows, a cat looks on, / In candy colors, the girls are gone.
“Do you know what you have done?” A Hammer classic with a French duke battling a charismatic satanist, a pentacle circle and the Angel of Death.
Who am I? — A 1968 British picture set in the English Civil War, where Vincent Price plays a self-appointed hunter of witches who tortures for money.

A vengeful organist, masked and thin, / Kills surgeons by the plagues of sin;
Locusts, frogs, and rats and blood, / To Egypt’s curse he gives the flood.
“Parting is such sweet sorrow.” A hammy Shakespearean actor, thought dead, kills the critics who spurned him by staging the deaths from the Bard’s plays.
Who am I? — A grieving family’s son returns from Vietnam after a mother’s plea, but he’s silent, pale and needs a dreadful supply to stay alive.

A Californian seaside town in dread, / A painter’s father gone and fled;
A moon of blood, a cinema’s seats, / Where pale-faced townsfolk feed on meats.
Who am I? — A young woman recently out of a mental hospital moves to a Connecticut farmhouse, where a strange drifter and a pale girl seem to know her.
“I want you to help me.” A grieving composer in a rented Seattle mansion hears bangs on the pipes and finds a small wheelchair in a sealed room.
Who am I? — A rental house offered at a bargain for a summer holiday, which seems to heal itself and slowly drain its tenants while consuming an obsessive wife.

A single mother, nightly prey, / To unseen force that will not stay;
The doctors say it’s in her mind, / But parapsychs find what’s not kind.
“Rage made flesh.” A radical psychotherapist’s patient births small, furious children at his retreat, and they attack those who anger her.
Who am I? — A glossy Montreal tower block where a scientist’s experimental parasite turns residents into lustful, ravenous carriers, in Cronenberg’s early feature.

A pirate signal, torture play, / A slit across the belly’s way;
A tape inside the stomach slips: / “Long live the new flesh!” on his lips.
Who am I? — After experimental plastic surgery, a woman grows a stinger from her armpit that feeds on blood, and a plague spreads through Montreal.
“Her features have been destroyed.” A surgeon abducts young women for transplant attempts to restore his daughter, who hides behind an expressionless white mask.
Who am I? — A 1955 Clouzot thriller where a headmaster’s wife and mistress drown him in a bathtub, after which his body vanishes from the pool.

A camera whirs, a tripod’s blade, / A mirror shows what fear has made;
He films the moment of their death, / A father’s lab gave him this breath.
“It’s only a cat.” A publicity stunt in a New Mexico town goes wrong when a circus cat breaks loose and the killings that follow may not be its doing.
Who am I? — A 1942 Val Lewton chiller in which a Serbian-born woman fears that kissing her husband will turn her into a panther; a swimming pool scene is famous.

A nurse from Canada, sugar isle, / Her patient walks in silent style;
The drums at night, the trail of stone, / A Jane Eyre story, voodoo-grown.
Who am I? — Boris Karloff plays a cabman who supplies Edinburgh doctors with fresh cadavers from unfortunate people, in this 1945 Val Lewton drama.
“There is a vorvolaka among us.” A Greek general quarantined with refugees on a small island suspects a vampiric spirit among the survivors.
Who am I? — A 1932 Tod Browning film in which a trapeze artist plots to poison a little person for his inheritance, and a carnival troupe takes revenge.

A Welsh road washed out by rain, / A brooding family in the lane;
A scarred and mute and drunken man / Controls the keys — the storms began.
“She is dead, yet she lives.” Bela Lugosi’s Haitian sugar-mill master, with a hypnotic stare, enslaves a bride so that a planter may have her.
Who am I? — A 1932 Carl Dreyer picture in which a young traveler at an inn sees shadows that move without bodies and an elderly lady spreading a curse.

A fairground showman, tall and stern, / A sleepwalker for whom they yearn;
With jagged sets and painted shade, / Expressionism’s first parade.
“Witchcraft through the ages.” A 1922 Swedish-Danish silent film mixing documentary lecture with dramatized sabbaths, torture chambers and demons.
Who am I? — A concert pianist who loses his fingers in a train wreck and is given those of an executed murderer, and finds them craving the knife.

A motel room, a clown in white, / A killer family on the flight;
To a Lynyrd Skynyrd guitar solo, / They run toward the end in the slow-mo.
Who am I? — A shy assistant at an animal hospital who was given a doll as a child and decides to build a perfect friend from the best parts of people.
“Hello, Doctor.” An asbestos-removal crew works in an abandoned Massachusetts asylum, and one worker listens to tapes of a patient with multiple personalities.
Who am I? — A British army squad on a training exercise in the Scottish Highlands, holed up in a farmhouse and besieged by a pack of werewolves.

A prom night snatched, a dinner set, / A father’s dress of pink, and yet;
A girl in sequins, spiked with glee, / Adores a boy tied to a tree.
“That’s not a knife.” Backpackers visiting a crater in the Australian outback accept help from a friendly stranger with a bush hat and a sinister garage.
Who am I? — Four British friends hiking a Swedish forest in memory of a lost friend take a shortcut and discover a horned, antlered figure worshipped by a cult.

A Welsh isle’s cult, a ransomed maid, / A goddess fed on blood and shade;
In nineteen-oh-five, a brother goes / To rescue her from savage foes.
Who am I? — A fifteenth-century Alpine tale of a lonely woman shunned as a witch, her baby, a goat’s milk and visions slowly consuming her mind.
“Something’s wrong with Mom.” Two siblings return to their parents’ remote Texas farm to say goodbye to their father and meet an unwelcome presence.
Who am I? — A 2020 film that opens with American hikers in a Bulgarian mountain pass and later follows a retired cop hunting for a missing girl and a cult.

A grandmother’s house, a note on a door, / Black mold spreads across the floor;
Three generations, one dark maze, / Of dementia’s slow and eerie haze.
Who am I? — A 2017 Indonesian remake in which a family with a dying singer is visited by dread after the mother’s death and her old fan group returns.
“That’s not my son.” A mother in rural Ireland suspects her boy has changed after discovering a vast sinkhole in the forest nearby.
Who am I? — A grieving woman hires a grim occultist to guide her through a months-long ritual in a remote Welsh house to speak to her dead son.

A family films a teenage girl, / Who drowned and left a puzzling swirl;
The tapes reveal what she concealed, / In Australian mockumentary revealed.
“Who’s hungry?” A reunion dinner in the Hollywood Hills with his ex-wife and her new husband, who has joined a strange group, turns unsettling.
Who am I? — A roadside wax museum where mannequins move on their own; the owner, played by Chuck Connors, has an odd telekinetic talent.

A Brooklyn brownstone, flats above, / A blind old priest sits at the door;
A model rents a room there, then / Discovers Hell lies in that den.
Who am I? — A 1987 John Carpenter film in which physics students and a priest in an L.A. church study a swirling green canister that holds the Anti-God.
“Read my books.” An insurance investigator is sent to find a missing best-selling horror writer and ends up in a town that exists only in his fiction.
Who am I? — A centennial in a California coastal town, when a glowing mist rolls in carrying the vengeful ghosts of drowned lepers from a wrecked ship.

Two sisters sworn to die as one, / One bitten when the night is done;
Her body changes with the moon, / And suburbs hear the howling tune.
“They’re all infected!” A bioweapon contaminates the water of a Pennsylvania town, and soldiers in white suits seal it off from the world.
Who am I? — A 1961 Roger Corman film, based on a Poe story, in which a man visits a Spanish castle after his sister’s death and finds torture devices.

w: THE MASQUE OF THE RED DEATH
c:
A prince behind his castle wall, / Throws a party for them all;
Seven rooms in seven hues, / A cloaked guest nobody excuses.
Who am I? — A Hammer film from 1971 in which two identical sisters come to live with a puritan uncle and a decadent count, one good and one corrupted.
“Carmilla is my name.” A young general’s daughter befriends a mysterious guest whose arrival coincides with a series of deaths in Styria.
Who am I? — A 1970 vampire in Los Angeles, played by Robert Quarry, who arrives with a coffin and a séance to claim a young woman.

An architect with a dream he knew, / A ventriloquist’s dummy, too;
Five tales are told one stormy eve, / The circle ends where you believe.
“Do you smell mimosa?” A brother and sister buy a bargain seaside house in Cornwall and find a spirit, cold spots and a scent of flowers.
Who am I? — A Halloween night in 1962 when a small boy locked in the school cloakroom witnesses the ghost of a murdered girl and meets a killer.

Old men in a New England town, / Sit by the fire as the snow comes down;
They tell their tales to keep at bay, / A woman they once did away.
“It’s only a movie.” A TV anchor recovers at a rural retreat, the Colony, whose members seem to share a savage secret in the woods.
Who am I? — An Oklahoma farm boy lured by a pretty drifter is bitten and forced to live on the road with a nomadic family of blood-drinkers.

A burlap-masked and lollipop'd tot, / Enforces all the rules he's got;
One Ohio town, one Halloween night, / Four stories tangled up in fright.
“Who’s killing the campers?” A shy girl arrives at Arawak summer retreat with her cousin, and a string of 'accidents' ends in one of horror’s most notorious twists.
Who am I? — A found-footage film in which a Maryland town’s Fourth of July celebration is overrun by parasites released by the polluted water.

In England’s fields, a plough turns up / A skull with fur — the earth’s dark cup;
The village children change and prey, / To summon back old Satan’s sway.
Who am I? — A 1970 Vincent Price film in which a cruel English magistrate hunts witches and is cursed by a wronged woman who sends a beast.
“Supernatural, perhaps. Baloney, perhaps not.” Karloff and Lugosi duel in a modernist Hungarian mansion built over a battlefield grave.
Who am I? — A loan officer denies an old woman an extension and is cursed by a demon named Lamia, with only three days left to escape damnation.

A painter, wife and metalhead child, / Move to a Texas farm so wild;
The old man’s voice commands the brush, / To paint what terrifies the hush.
“They’re not coming from there. They’re coming from inside.” A rural hospital is surrounded by hooded white figures as patients mutate within.
Who am I? — A meteorite lands on a farm and its shimmering pink hue warps the well, the alpacas, the plants and the family, in a Lovecraft adaptation.

A couple lost on country lanes, / A hotel booked for their remains;
The signs repeat, the roads all bend, / And someone watches round each end.
Who am I? — Vatican investigators arrive at a remote Devon church to debunk a reported miracle, and something in the crypt does not want them to.
“Thank you.” A depressed ex-soldier turned hitman takes a job with three targets, and with each murder, a sinister cult comes closer.
Who am I? — A traveling entertainer’s van breaks down in the Belgian Ardennes, where a lonely innkeeper decides that he will never leave.

w: ALL THE BOYS LOVE MANDY LANE
c:
A Texas ranch, a party night, / A girl all others hold in sight;
The guests are picked off one by one, / To find who’s hiding with a gun.
